title: turns the 12-hour clock into the 24-hour one at both ends of the day
why: 12 AM read as 12 and 12 PM as 24: a Made written just after midnight or noon would name another hour, and the comparison with the record would fail on a moment that is the same.

title: reads the narrow no-break space ICU puts before AM
why: Only the plain space read: the narrow no-break space Chromium's ICU puts before AM would make every 0.1.0 Made unreadable, and step 22 would fail on a runner whose strip is right.

find: const [, month, day, year, hour, minute, second, meridiem] = numeric
replace: const [, day, month, year, hour, minute, second, meridiem] = numeric
title: reads 0.1.0's toLocaleString, with its seconds
why: 0.1.0's en-US date read day first: the thirteenth of November would be refused as a thirteenth month, and an earlier day misread as another.

title: reads the later versions' words, with no seconds, in either hour cycle
why: The month in words read one short: November would be October, and Made after the update would never be the moment 0.1.0 wrote.

title: is false for another minute, another day, another second, or words it cannot read
why: Minutes not compared: a Made a minute or an hour's part away would pass as unchanged.

title: to the second where the words give one, and to the minute always
why: Seconds never compared where both texts give them: 0.1.0's strip could disagree with its own record by seconds and the seed would not say.

title: refuses what is not JSON, another record, and phases it does not know
why: An upgrade.json of another shape read as this one: a later phase would compare with fields that mean something else.

title: refuses a phase that does not say whether it passed, or passed with problems
why: A phase that says it passed while listing problems would be taken at its word.

title: refuses a seed with a field missing or of the wrong kind
why: A seed whose export hash is not one: after's "the post is unchanged" would compare a hash with anything and fail for the wrong reason, or a blank would be kept.

title: fails on a step of the workflow that did not succeed, whatever its word
why: A skipped or cancelled install read as fine: step 22 could pass with the release never installed over 0.1.0.

title: fails on a phase that wrote nothing, or did not pass
why: A phase that never wrote its verdict - back never ran - passes the row.

find: if (!ran.ok && ran.problems.length === 0) problems.push(`${phase}: did not pass`)
title: fails on a phase that wrote nothing, or did not pass
why: A phase written as failed with no problem named would pass the row.

title: replaces one field's value, redacted, and leaves the others
why: A field written unredacted: a path in it would reach the public issue the record is pasted into.

find: const record = fillField(readRecord(recordPath), 'Previous version installed', previous)
title: writes the row and the previous version into the record the spec wrote
why: The run table would go on saying the previous version is not known after the workflow installed 0.1.0 under the release.

title: writes a failure, and exits 1, where a phase failed or nothing was written down
why: A failed step 22 written into the record with a green workflow step.
